newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to remove controversial London envoy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to remove controversial London envoy.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo has ordered the removal of Mexico's ambassador to London, a veteran diplomat who analysts said may have earned Zedillo's wrath for being too close to the president's political opponents.

Andres Rozental, a diplomatic officer for 33 years who was a former deputy foreign minister, said in a telephone interview from London on Monday that he had not sought reasons for being recalled, and declined to speculate what they may have been.

But Mexico's Epoca news magazine, in its Monday cover story, said Rozental may have fallen foul of what it called Zedillo's "Firm Hand" in the new year, because of his links to his half-brother Jorge Castaneda, a vocal critic of Zedillo's government who is also a respected political analyst.

"I was told that the president had decided to name somebody else (as ambassador) and I decided I would seek a leave of absence from the foreign service for an indefinite period," Rozental told Reuters.
It was not clear when he would return to Mexico. A Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said she had no comment on his situation.

Zedillo, a publicity-shy technocrat not known for fiery speeches, stunned analysts last week by lashing out at unnamed critics -- many suspected including Castaneda -- who he accused of "feeding a mistaken image of the country."

In a speech to Mexican ambassadors at which Rozental was present last week, Zedillo attacked a small group of Mexicans who he said "meet with (foreign) correspondents to receive them in their homes at the weekend until they convince them that Mexico will go on being ... the perfect dictatorship."

Not coincidentally, at the time of Zedillo's speech, Castaneda was organising a barbecue lunch with foreign correspondents on Sunday to promote a political alliance against the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
The PRI has been in power for 67 years, and Castaneda and others were seeking to forge a coalition of opposition parties to defeat it in mid-term elections in July.

"It seems a bit suspicious to me that in the same week that a group proposes an opposition coalition, and that Zedillo reproaches analysts for presenting a bad image (of his government), the half-brother of Jorge Castaneda is removed from his post," said Jose Antonio Crespo, a political analyst who attended Sunday's lunch. "It is not a casual connection."

Epoca said Rozental may have been ousted because of an embarrassing incident last May in which Castaneda had a meeting in Dublin with disgraced former President Carlos Salinas that was leaked to the Mexican press.
Following that meeting, Mexico's ambassador to Dublin, Agustin Gutierrez Canet, was removed from his post, even though he denied fixing the meeting.
Other analysts speculated Rozental may have been forced out because he sometimes entertained anti-PRI politicians in London as well as pro-government figures.
